findings.title: UniPoolerV2 'Overflow bound' NatSpec still justifies _swapAmount's checked product by uint112 reserves and a balance cap, neither of which holds for quotePool after 267660b
findings.primaryWriteUp: CODE-21-001 (strict superset: adds the 'a is capped by this contract's sUSDS balance' half, which never held for quotePool and predates this diff). LOCAL-Q-01 is the profiler's narrower statement of the uint112 half.
findings.description: The 'Overflow bound' NatSpec bounds _swapAmount's checked product with two claims: 'V2 reserves are uint112' and 'a is capped by this contract's sUSDS balance'. After 267660b, quotePool feeds _swapAmount uint256 balanceOf(pair) values (:502, :531-533), not uint112 reserves. quotePool also never caps sUSDSIn by the contract balance (its own @dev says it can quote hypothetical amounts), so the second claim has never held for quotePool. pool() still satisfies both: sync() reverts above uint112, and :459 caps a.
findings.attackVector: None. Checked arithmetic: an out-of-range quotePool input reverts, never wraps. pool() is still bounded (sync() reverts above uint112; :459 caps a).
findings.recommendation: Scope the bound to pool(): sync() enforces uint112 and the balance check caps a. State that quotePool takes uint256 balances and arbitrary sUSDSIn and relies on checked arithmetic to revert.

findings.title: UniPoolerV2 'The zap' NatSpec and story-051 misstate the donation mechanism and beneficiary: an unsynced donation was never 'absorbed into our swap and LP mint' and does not accrue 'overwhelmingly' to this contract's POL by code guarantee
findings.primaryWriteUp: F-02-051 (covers both halves: the 'absorbed into our swap/mint' mechanism error and the 'overwhelmingly this contract's POL' beneficiary premise, plus the live feeTo 1/6 share). ECON-21-001 supplies the economic proof (router fixes amountOut from stored reserves; swap() credits s+D; _update folds D into reserves for every LP; pre-fix strand was protocol inventory, ~103 phUSD in the 0.5%/100k simulation, not donated value) and answers CODE-21-003's open custody question from the plan (BalancerWinddownPlan.md:375/:472: seed addLiquidity mints to UniPoolerV2). CODE-21-003 is the narrower 'overwhelmingly POL is an operational assumption' facet of the same NatSpec line.
findings.mechanismCorrection: Without a sync, the router fixes amountOut from the stale reserves. The donation only enlarges swap()'s computed amountIn, which loosens the K check, and swap()'s _update() then folds it into the reserves. The pooler receives nothing extra from the swap or the mint. The stranding comes from the router's _addLiquidity quoting against the shifted post-swap reserves while s was sized on the stale ones. In both cases (unsynced pre-fix, and synced post-fix) the donation accrues pro-rata to the LP holders that existed before our mint. Because mainnet V2 feeTo is ON (0xf385...5f85) and sync() does not touch kLast, feeTo also takes about 1/6 of the sqrt(k) growth the donation causes at the next mint/burn, our own addLiquidity included. 'Overwhelmingly this contract's POL' holds only to the extent that UniPoolerV2 holds the pre-existing LP. The cutover seed LP recipient is set by the phStaging2 script, not this contract.
findings.beneficiaryNote: Pro rata to LP holders before our mint, minus feeTo's ~1/6 of sqrt(k) growth (feeTo LIVE, see DEDUP-21-05). 'Overwhelmingly POL' holds only if UniPoolerV2 custodies the seed LP; that is set by the phStaging2 script (plan says it does), not enforced in code.
findings.economicImpact: None. The donation was never protocol value; donor loses (1-g)*D. Fix verdict for L-25 is not challenged.
findings.recommendation: Reword the NatSpec as: 'without a sync, a donation is folded into reserves by swap()'s _update after s was sized on the stale reserves, so addLiquidity's optimal-amount selection no longer matches the two legs. Syncing first folds it before sizing. Either way the donation accrues pro-rata to existing LP holders (and to feeTo's protocol-fee share).' Also (ECON-21-001): phase-2 Stage 2 verification should assert pair.balanceOf(UniPoolerV2) == pair.totalSupply() - 1000 - pair.balanceOf(feeTo). Mirror the correction into story-051 Background / Implementation Notes (product-owner; read-only here).

findings.title: story-051 silently supersedes story-048's 'mint path kept verbatim / identical dispatcher' clause: UniPoolerV2._dispatch now differs from BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch by the HookNotSet guard, and story-048 still asserts the verbatim clause
findings.description: With comments stripped, _dispatch differs from BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch by exactly one statement: `if (address(hook) == _defaultHook) revert UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet();`. _psmDonate differs only in revert-string prefixes. An un-hooked UniPoolerV2 now reverts every index-4 mint, where BalancerPoolerV2 would silently accrue zero debt, so 'identical dispatcher' no longer holds until setHook is called. The contract @dev header was reworded honestly (story-051 Autonomous Decision 8).
findings.deviation: Story-048's verbatim/identical-dispatcher clause is superseded by story-051, which explicitly mandates the guard as the first line of UniPoolerV2._dispatch. The later, owner-directed spec wins, so this is not a Law-2 violation of the code. But story-051 never states that it waives 048's clause, and the 048 document still asserts it. A reader grading against 048 alone would raise a false deviation.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line supersession note to story-048 (or 051): 'the _dispatch verbatim clause is amended by story-051: the hook-not-set guard is the only behavioural difference'. No code change.
findings.relatedPrior: Run-20 DEDUP-20-01 law2Annotation explicitly asked for this waiver to be recorded if the in-_dispatch guard was adopted. It was adopted (L-21 fix) but the waiver was not written; this finding is that follow-through.

findings.title: Uniswap V2 fee switch is LIVE on the mainnet factory (feeTo 0xf385...5f85); quotePool's NatSpec treats fee-on as hypothetical and code-scan MR-004 cleared the sync()/feeTo interaction on the false premise 'feeTo is off'
findings.partialMergeFrom: PATTERN-MR-002 first half (quotePool totalSupply excludes the _mintFee LP; divergence errs safe). The TOCTOU half of PATTERN-MR-002 is routed to LEDGER-COVERED LC-21-01.

premiseCorrection.falseClaim: code-scan MR-004: 'feeTo is off on the mainnet V2 factory' (disposition 'cleared').
premiseCorrection.correctedFact: cast call 0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f feeTo() returned 0xf38521f130fcCF29dB1961597bc5d2B60F995f85 at scan time (UNIfication, Dec 2025; BalancerWinddownPlan.md:174 already records it). feeTo is governance-mutable.
premiseCorrection.why: feeTo takes at most 1/6 of sqrt(k) growth since kLast (donation- and fee-driven). LP value never falls below its pre-growth level; minted LP >= quote, so minLP remains a valid unit floor. Fork tests on the real feeTo-on pair assert LP >= quote (faithfulness 051-T).
premiseCorrection.directive: Downstream agents and later runs must carry the corrected premise; do not inherit 'feeTo is off' from MR-004.

findings.description: Code-scan MR-004 cleared the feeTo interaction with sync() on the premise 'feeTo is off on the mainnet V2 factory'. That premise is false. `cast call 0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f feeTo()` returns 0xf38521f130fcCF29dB1961597bc5d2B60F995f85 today, and BalancerWinddownPlan.md:174 already records it as live (UNIfication, Dec 2025). Consequences: (a) at the zap's addLiquidity, _mintFee mints feeTo about 1/6 of the sqrt(k) growth since kLast. That growth includes any donation folded in by sync() (and, pre-fix, by swap) and the swap fees. (b) quotePool computes expectedLP from the pre-fee totalSupply. The fee-on branch of its NatSpec is therefore the live case, not a hypothetical. Our minted LP count is ≥ the quote, so minLP is still a valid floor in LP units, but each LP unit carries the feeTo dilution.
findings.economicImpact: Negligible, and no loss of protocol principal. feeTo takes at most 1/6 of the growth, so LP value never falls below its pre-growth level. Swap-fee growth of about 0.15%·V/R_side per traded volume V gives a feeTo share of about 0.025% of supply per one-side-reserve of volume. A donation D yields about D/(12·rS) of supply to feeTo, all of it donated value. The 0.30% swap fee and therefore phusdOut are unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Update the quotePool NatSpec to say the V2 fee switch is on and expectedLP is therefore a conservative unit floor. Have the setAside record carry the corrected premise so later runs do not inherit 'feeTo is off'.
